summary: Iteration 4 — covered the new Proctored OA + Admin unban features end-to-end. Backend: wrote /app/backend/tests/test_proctor_admin.py (15 tests, all passing, 35s). Covers admin login/role, 403 on admin routes for non-admin, 401 for unauth, /admin/stats shape, /admin/bans filters (active/lifted/all) with active flag, /admin/users list + search + admin excluded, create-ban-via-duplicate-register → active ban appears → POST /admin/bans/{id}/unban → double-unban returns 400 → POST /admin/users/{id}/unban idempotent → banned user can log in again (full round-trip verified, cleanup in finally so IP ban can never leak). Proctored OA generate returns proctored:true, all 8 FLAG_WEIGHTS flag types accepted, unknown rejected 400, submit returns proctoring {integrity_score, risk, counts, timeline} with integrity<100 after flags and auto_reason echoed, further flags after submit return recorded:false. Non-proctored OA regression: proctored:false and proctoring:null on submit. Frontend (Playwright): test1 login works, nav-admin hidden for non-admin, /admin redirects non-admin to /dashboard. Mock OA page shows oa-proctor-toggle (aria-checked flips to true), Generate OA with proctored on routes to proctor-setup system-check (does NOT call /mock-oa/generate yet — generation deferred to after fullscreen, which is the correct UX). proctor-allow-btn visible; headless Chromium granted fake media so proctor-start-btn appeared (proctor-error path not exercised but is coded correctly). Logout → admin login → nav-admin visible → /admin shows all 4 admin-stat cards (users/banned_users/active_bans/lifted_bans), admin-tab-bans + admin-tab-users, bans-filter-active/lifted/all all present and clickable, users table renders test1 row. Lifted bans count = 2 (one pre-existing + the one this run created and lifted), active bans = 0 after cleanup.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_prep.proctor_report: uses `FLAG_WEIGHTS[k]` directly inside sum() — if an unknown key ever lands in flags (e.g. legacy data or future bugs), this raises KeyError and submit 500s. Current oa_flag endpoint validates, so this is safe today, but a `.get(k, 0)` guard is a one-line hardening.
routes_prep.oa_flag query uses `flags.299` to cap at 300 flags — subtle but works; worth a comment or constant.

auth.is_banned OR query includes `{'ip': ip}` even when env flag disabled only in the branch logic — the final filter mixes $or with `active: {$ne: False}` at the same level which Mongo evaluates correctly (both are top-level AND), but a nested $and would be clearer.

routes_admin._lift updates users to banned:false AFTER setting bans inactive, but if a user has multiple active bans only the single targeted ban is lifted when calling /bans/{id}/unban — the condition `if not await db.bans.find_one(...)` correctly keeps user banned if other active bans remain. Good.

MockOA.js: when proctor fails inside submit() (catch branch), it calls begin(test.id) which re-opens camera/mic — if the test was already auto-submitted for integrity, this re-captures media; low priority but a UX quirk.
ProctorSetup: no handling for the 'camera track present but video is black' case (common with virtual cameras) — camera_blocked flag relies on monitor loop. Acceptable.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all data-testid elements present and interactive; redirect, toggle, admin stats/tabs/filters all verified)

seed_data_creation: Backend test created and generated 2 mock OA sessions for test1 (1 proctored submitted, 1 non-proctored submitted) and created-then-lifted 1 ban. After this run active_bans=0, lifted_bans=2 (prior lifted + this one), 2 extra mock OA attempts in test1 history.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suites: /app/backend/tests/test_backend.py, test_new_features.py, test_proctor_admin.py. The proctor+admin suite is safe to re-run (finally block always unbans test1). Chromium in this env has fake media available, so proctor-start-btn path works in headless — proctor-error path only triggers if request() rejects.
